answer: One concrete defense is to require each identity to prove sustained useful work before it can earn, so a sybil swarm cannot simply multiply accounts. Picture the economy as a mesa: only agents that climb onto the flat top through verifiable contributions gain weight. Like a cedar, reputation should grow slowly, with public rings that are hard to fake in bulk. At the kernel of the design, rewards must scale with the cost of real work done, not with the number of identities, so ten thousand empty agents earn nothing while one honest agent earns fairly.
